Alfa Romeo|Giulia.v: Facelifted in 2023, the Giulia remains one of the most enjoyable saloons to drive in its class. A noisy diesel, an austere cabin and the complete absence of hybridisation hold it back.
p: Incisive chassis, good balance of comfort and dynamism
m: Austere cabin, infotainment slightly behind the times
No hybrid powertrain, not even a mild hybrid
Diesel noisy at start-up and at high revs
Alfa Romeo|Giulia.q: Keen drivers who want a diesel saloon
Alfa Romeo|Giulia.s: Facelifted for 2023: Tonale-inspired LED headlights, smoked rear lights and digital instruments.

Alfa Romeo|Junior.v: Alfa Romeo's first small SUV, the Junior stands out for its styling and a genuinely fun electric Veloce. It shares its underpinnings with the Jeep Avenger and Peugeot 2008, and it is expensive.
p: Lively Veloce thanks to its limited-slip differential
Choice of hybrid, Q4 hybrid or electric
m: Hard plastics, screen set too low
High prices, especially for the electric version
Alfa Romeo|Junior.q: City dwellers who want a small SUV with Italian style
Alfa Romeo|Junior.s: It was meant to be called Milano: the name was dropped just before launch in favour of Junior, an Alfa Romeo name from the 1960s.
Alfa Romeo|Junior.x: The 1.2 Ibrida 145 hp is willing without being sporty; the Q4 adds traction. The Elettrica 280 hp (Veloce) is the most fun, but its range drops quickly when driven hard.

Alfa Romeo|Stelvio.v: Thanks to its steering and chassis, the Stelvio remains one of the most enjoyable SUVs to drive in its class. Build quality, infotainment, a noisy diesel and the lack of a hybrid count against it next to its German rivals.
Alfa Romeo|Stelvio.q: Demanding drivers looking for a dynamic diesel SUV
Alfa Romeo|Stelvio.s: Facelifted for 2023: Tonale-inspired Matrix LED headlights, smoked rear lights and fully digital instruments.

Alfa Romeo|Tonale.v: A neatly styled compact SUV, the facelifted Tonale is agile through corners, especially as a Q4 plug-in hybrid. Over-assisted steering and a lack of character deny it the sportiness expected of an Alfa Romeo.
m: Smaller boot in the plug-in hybrid
High consumption with a flat battery
Alfa Romeo|Tonale.q: Fans of Italian style looking for a compact SUV
Alfa Romeo|Tonale.s: Facelifted for 2026: revised front end and rotary gear selector. In the Q4 plug-in hybrid, the battery cuts boot space from 500 to 385 litres.
Alfa Romeo|Tonale.x: The 1.6 Mjet II 130 hp is the most rational choice; the 1.5 Ibrida 175 hp stands out for its smoothness; the Ibrida Plug-In Q4 270 hp is the liveliest but loses boot space.

Alpine|A290.v: The sporty version of the Renault 5, named European Car of the Year 2025 alongside it. Effective chassis and classy presentation, but an electric motor short on character, limited range when driven hard and a high price.
p: Classy presentation, distinct from the R5
Brembo brakes from the A110, supportive seats
Alpine|A290.q: Drivers who want everyday sportiness, especially in and around town
Alpine|A290.s: Named European Car of the Year 2025 jointly with the Renault 5 E-Tech, whose 52 kWh battery it shares.
Alpine|A290.x: The Electric 220 hp is about a second quicker from 0-100 km/h than the Electric 180 hp, but gives up a little range because of its wider tyres and extra weight.

Alpine|A390.v: A three-motor electric family sports car, praised for its agility despite weighing more than two tonnes. Comfortable and remarkably well damped, it is let down by high consumption and below-par charging.
m: Patchy build quality, some poor plastics
Alpine|A390.q: Families of keen drivers ready to go electric
Alpine|A390.s: It sits on the AmpR Medium platform of the electric Renault Mégane and Scénic, with one front motor and two rear motors providing torque vectoring.
Alpine|A390.x: The Electric 400 hp (GT) keeps the same chassis for around €10,500 less; the Electric 470 hp (GTS) is noticeably quicker and charges faster (190 kW vs 150 kW).

Audi|A2 e-tron.v: A premium electric hatchback reviving the A2 name, built on the MEB+ platform of the VW ID.3 and Cupra Born. Prototype drives praise its efficiency, less so its firm suspension; it costs more than its cousins.
p: Remarkable efficiency according to early drives
Long range with the larger battery
m: Little hindsight: only prototypes driven so far
Audi|A2 e-tron.q: Drivers wanting a premium, long-range electric hatchback
Audi|A2 e-tron.s: Built in Ingolstadt (Germany). First deliveries announced for December 2026. Versions under €47,000 should qualify for the French EV incentive (CEE scheme).
Audi|A2 e-tron.x: The e-tron 190 hp offers adequate in-gear pace without spectacular acceleration; the e-tron 231 hp and e-tron 326 hp get a bigger battery, which extends range and speeds up charging.

Audi|A3 Allstreet.v: A version of the A3 Sportback raised by 3 cm, with rugged looks but no all-wheel drive. It keeps its precise steering, at the cost of firmer suspension and a premium that is mostly cosmetic.
p: Classy cabin, roomy outer rear seats
Audi|A3 Allstreet.q: Fans of rugged looks who want to keep hatchback dimensions
Audi|A3 Allstreet.s: Introduced with the 2024 facelift: ground clearance raised by 3 cm, front-wheel drive only, priced €1,400-1,900 above the equivalent A3 Sportback.
Audi|A3 Allstreet.x: The 2.0 TDI S-Tronic 150 hp is far more pleasant: better insulated, punchier and more frugal. The 1.5 TFSI Hybrid S-Tronic 150 hp lacks punch and gets noisy under acceleration.

Audi|A3 Berline.v: The three-box version of the A3, facelifted in 2024, has a bigger boot than the Sportback (425 l vs 380 l). Agile and frugal, it falls down on limited rear headroom and a characterless petrol engine.
p: Low consumption as a mild hybrid
m: Centre rear seat hampered by the tunnel
Audi|A3 Berline.q: Fans of the classic compact saloon with a separate boot
Audi|A3 Berline.s: Facelifted in 2024 and priced €565 above the Sportback. Rivals: BMW 2 Series Gran Coupé and Mercedes A-Class saloon.
Audi|A3 Berline.x: The 1.5 TFSI 150 hp versions, flexible from low revs, are What Car?'s recommended choice; the torquier 2.0 TDI S-Tronic 150 hp is more relaxed on the motorway.

Audi|A3 Sportback.v: Facelifted in 2024, the A3 Sportback appeals with its precise handling and economy, but a patchy, austere cabin and prices among the highest in the class take the shine off.
Audi|A3 Sportback.q: Drivers seeking a premium hatchback that is well rounded on the road
Audi|A3 Sportback.s: 2024 facelift: revised front end and customisable daytime light signatures (four patterns). Rivals: BMW 1 Series and Mercedes A-Class.
Audi|A3 Sportback.x: The 2.0 TDI S-Tronic 150 hp is judged more pleasant than the 150 hp petrols: stronger in-gear acceleration and a quieter note, while the petrol gets noisy at high revs.

Audi|A5.v: Replacing the A4, the A5 hides a hatchback beneath its saloon lines. Quiet and frugal as a diesel, it disappoints with uncommunicative steering, a heavily touch-based interface and expensive options.
p: Quiet and refined on long journeys
Audi|A5.q: High-mileage drivers seeking a comfortable, frugal premium saloon
Audi|A5.s: Under Audi's new naming scheme, the A5 succeeds both the A4 saloon and the A5 Sportback. Designated rival: the BMW 3 Series, which is more engaging to drive.
Audi|A5.x: The 2.0 TFSI 150 hp is adequate without being eager; the 2.0 TFSI 204 hp, preferred by What Car?, is livelier; the 2.0 TDI Hybrid 204 hp offers the strongest in-gear acceleration and good economy.

Audi|A5 Avant.v: The estate replacing the A4 Avant is quiet, comfortable and frugal as a diesel, but its boot lags behind its rivals', it lacks flavour to drive and almost all its controls go through the screen.
p: Quiet and refined on the motorway
m: Boot smaller than its BMW and Mercedes rivals'
Touch interface less practical than before
Lifeless steering, less agile than a 3 Series
Audi|A5 Avant.q: Families or high-mileage drivers seeking a premium estate
Audi|A5 Avant.s: The A5 Avant replaces the A4 Avant. Rivals: BMW 3 Series Touring and Mercedes C-Class Estate, the latter narrowly beaten in L'argus's group test.
Audi|A5 Avant.x: The 2.0 TFSI 150 hp feels sluggish, the 2.0 TFSI 204 hp is livelier; the 2.0 TDI Hybrid 204 hp, the most frugal, is Carbuyer's pick, with the Quattro version adding traction.

Audi|A6.v: The sixth generation, launched in 2025: a highly aerodynamic saloon, comfortable and designed for high-mileage drivers. Boot behind its rivals', cramped centre seat, firm suspension and a high price.
Audi|A6.q: High-mileage diesel loyalists seeking a premium cruiser
Audi|A6.s: Sold alongside the electric A6 e-tron; two plug-in hybrids complement the diesel. Rivals: BMW 5 Series and Mercedes E-Class.
Audi|A6.x: The 2.0 TDI Hybrid 204 hp is considered very smooth; the 2.0 e-hybrid Quattro S-Tronic 299 hp, lively and competitively priced against the diesel, sacrifices a good chunk of boot space and feels rough under acceleration.

Audi|A6 Avant.v: The sixth-generation A6 estate (2025): agile despite its weight, quiet and comfortable, with a refined mild-hybrid diesel. Boot merely adequate, disappointing plastics and heavy taxation.
p: Quiet and comfortable on long journeys
m: Boot smaller than the BMW 5 Series Touring's
High French malus tax and weight tax
Audi|A6 Avant.q: High-mileage families seeking a premium estate
Audi|A6 Avant.s: Sold alongside the electric A6 Avant e-tron. Rear-wheel steering and air suspension optional. Rivals: BMW 5 Series Touring and Mercedes E-Class Estate.

Audi|A6 Avant e-tron.v: An electric estate on the PPE platform: long range, rapid 800 V charging and the comfort of a grand tourer. A boot no bigger than the saloon's, lifeless steering and a high price take the edge off.
Audi|A6 Avant e-tron.q: Families or high-mileage drivers seeking a premium electric estate
Audi|A6 Avant e-tron.s: Cd of 0.24 vs 0.21 for the Sportback, with an identical boot. No rear-wheel steering, even as an option. Designated rival: BMW i5 Touring.
Audi|A6 Avant e-tron.x: The e-tron 285 hp, with a smaller battery, is mainly aimed at shorter journeys; the Performance e-tron 367 hp offers the longest range, while the Quattro e-tron 428 hp gives up a little.

Audi|A6 Sportback e-tron.v: A highly aerodynamic electric saloon on the PPE platform: range among the best on the market and rapid charging, but tight rear seats and patchy build quality for the price.
m: Optional camera mirrors of little use
Audi|A6 Sportback e-tron.q: High-mileage drivers switching to electric without giving up comfort
Audi|A6 Sportback e-tron.s: Cd of 0.21 with the camera mirrors. Rivals: BMW i5, Mercedes EQE and Porsche Taycan.
Audi|A6 Sportback e-tron.x: The rear-wheel-drive e-tron 285 hp is the most enjoyable to drive according to What Car?; the Performance e-tron 367 hp offers the best range; the Quattro e-tron 428 hp gains traction but loses a little range.

Audi|A8.v: The benchmark limousine for comfort and technology, but at the very end of its life: Audi stopped taking orders in Germany in February 2026, with no replacement for several years.
p: Very upmarket build quality and equipment
m: Steep depreciation, typical of the segment
Audi|A8.q: Executives or high-mileage drivers seeking a comfortable limousine
Audi|A8.s: Orders stopped in Germany in February 2026, with the end of production near. The electric replacement is not expected to be ready before 2029.

Audi|A8 L.v: The long-wheelbase A8, designed for rear passengers: first-rate space and comfort, but the model is at the end of its life and the hybrid system eats into the boot.
m: Model at the end of its career
Steep depreciation, typical of the segment
Audi|A8 L.q: Executives who are often chauffeured and travel in the back
Audi|A8 L.s: Orders stopped in Germany in February 2026, with the end of production near. The electric replacement is not expected to be ready before 2029.

Audi|Q2.v: An agile, well-built small premium SUV, but designed in 2016 and now at the end of its life: production ended in spring 2026 and only stock cars remain.
m: Rear seats and boot tight for a family
Dashboard dated next to recent rivals
Audi|Q2.q: City dwellers or couples after a small premium SUV from stock at a negotiated price
Audi|Q2.s: Production ended in April 2026: it can no longer be configured and only stock remains. Its de facto successor is the electric A2 e-tron, delivered from December 2026.

Audi|Q3.v: The third generation, renewed in 2025, moves clearly upmarket: classy build quality, careful sound insulation and a sliding rear bench. The price climbs quickly with options.
m: High prices, S line trim recommended
Audi|Q3.q: Families seeking a recent, quiet premium compact SUV
Audi|Q3.s: Reputedly strong residual values, which keep lease payments down. Rivals: BMW X1 and Mercedes GLA.
Audi|Q3.x: The smooth, quiet 1.5 TFSI Hybrid 150 hp is the best compromise for Parkers; the frugal, long-legged 2.0 TDI 150 hp targets high-mileage drivers; the 1.5 e-hybrid 272 hp covers long distances on electric power.

Audi|Q3 Sportback.v: The sloping-roof version of the new Q3 (2025): the same gains in build quality and insulation, a sportier silhouette and preserved interior space, at the cost of a price premium and a smaller boot.
m: Smaller boot, the least versatile Q3
Audi|Q3 Sportback.q: Style-conscious buyers with no need for maximum versatility
Audi|Q3 Sportback.s: Priced around €2,500 above the Q3 with the same engine. The plug-in hybrid remains front-wheel drive, without quattro, and does not escape the French weight-based malus tax.
Audi|Q3 Sportback.x: The 1.5 e-hybrid 272 hp, lively and rated for 120 km of electric range, costs €10,500 more than the 1.5 TFSI Hybrid 150 hp: a gap that takes a long time to recoup, especially outside company fleets.

Audi|Q4 Sportback e-tron.v: The coupé version of the Q4 e-tron, comfortable and pleasant to drive. The 2026 facelift modernises the cabin and improves efficiency; the rear window is still split by the spoiler and options are costly.
p: Good balance of comfort and agility
m: Rear visibility hampered by the spoiler
Rear drum brakes with a vague pedal feel
Audi|Q4 Sportback e-tron.q: Families drawn to coupé styling and ready for electric
Audi|Q4 Sportback e-tron.s: 2026 facelift: screens grouped under a single curved panel, entry-level battery increased to 59 kWh usable and bidirectional charging (V2L), a first for Audi.
Audi|Q4 Sportback e-tron.x: The rear-wheel-drive e-tron 285 hp is judged the best balanced; the Quattro e-tron 340 hp accelerates harder and has better traction, but costs considerably more and rides more firmly.

Audi|Q4 e-tron.v: A roomy electric family SUV that is pleasant to drive. The 2026 facelift modernises the cabin and improves efficiency, without getting rid of expensive options or high motorway consumption.
p: Good balance of comfort and agility
m: Rear drum brakes with a vague pedal feel
Audi|Q4 e-tron.q: Families switching to electric with a premium SUV
Audi|Q4 e-tron.s: 2026 facelift: screens grouped under a single curved panel, entry-level battery increased to 59 kWh usable and bidirectional charging (V2L), a first for Audi.
Audi|Q4 e-tron.x: The rear-wheel-drive e-tron 285 hp is judged the best balanced; the Quattro e-tron 340 hp accelerates harder and has better traction, but costs considerably more and rides more firmly.

Audi|Q5.v: The third generation on the PPC platform: modern cabin, smooth and frugal diesel, secure handling. Testers regret the firm suspension, too many touch controls and some disappointing materials for the price.
p: Good road manners for an SUV
m: Too many functions on the touchscreen
Some disappointing materials for the price
Audi|Q5.q: Families or high-mileage drivers seeking a versatile premium SUV
Audi|Q5.s: PPC platform shared with the new A5. 48 V mild hybrid system (18 kW motor) on the non-plug-in versions. Rivals: BMW X3 and Mercedes GLC.
Audi|Q5.x: The 2.0 TDI Hybrid 204 hp, smoother and much more frugal, is preferred to the 2.0 TFSI Hybrid 204 hp, which is lighter but noisy at high revs; the e-hybrid 299 hp impresses with its seamless hybrid system.

Audi|Q5 Sportback.v: The sloping-roof version of the new Q5: almost identical boot and rear space, the same smooth, frugal diesel, but a mostly cosmetic price premium and heavily touch-based controls.
p: Boot and rear seats close to the Q5's
m: Premium hard to justify over the Q5
Some disappointing materials for the price
Too many functions on the touchscreen
Audi|Q5 Sportback.q: Premium SUV buyers who put style first
Audi|Q5 Sportback.s: Launched in 2025 after the Q5 SUV, on the PPC platform shared with the new A5, with 48 V mild hybrid technology.
Audi|Q5 Sportback.x: The smooth, frugal 2.0 TDI Hybrid 204 hp is preferred to the 2.0 TFSI Hybrid 204 hp, which works less decisively with the gearbox and is noisy at high revs.

Audi|Q6 Sportback e-tron.v: The coupé version of the Q6 e-tron: quiet, comfortable, quick to charge and slightly longer-legged than the SUV, but rear headroom and boot space suffer, for a mostly cosmetic premium.
p: Slightly more range than the Q6
Audi|Q6 Sportback e-tron.q: Style-conscious high-mileage drivers ready for electric
Audi|Q6 Sportback e-tron.s: Roofline lowered by 37 mm compared with the Q6 e-tron, boot reduced to 511 litres. Designated rival: the electric Porsche Macan, more engaging to drive.
Audi|Q6 Sportback e-tron.x: The rear-wheel-drive Performance e-tron 306 hp is the recommended version for its range; the Quattro e-tron, uprated from 387 to 428 hp since the press drives, is only justified for traction or towing.

Audi|Q6 e-tron.v: Audi's first SUV on the PPE platform of the electric Porsche Macan: quiet, spacious and quick to charge, but with patchy build quality, a harsh ride in town and only average efficiency.
p: Quiet and comfortable on the motorway
m: Hard plastics unworthy of the price
Audi|Q6 e-tron.q: High-mileage drivers seeking a spacious premium electric SUV
Audi|Q6 e-tron.s: PPE platform shared with the electric Porsche Macan. Optional 10.9-inch passenger screen; 526-litre boot.
Audi|Q6 e-tron.x: The rear-wheel-drive Performance e-tron 306 hp offers the best range in the line-up; the Quattro e-tron, uprated from 387 to 428 hp since the press drives, is best kept for those who need the traction.

Audi|Q7.v: The new Q7 returns to classy build quality and offers great comfort on air suspension. Its V6 diesel, smooth but lacking verve for the price, uses a lot of fuel in real-world driving according to most tests.
p: Build quality and materials back to the very best
Lots of space in the first two rows
m: Sluggish, thirsty V6 diesel in real-world use
Audi|Q7.q: Well-off families who want a comfortable, well-built large seven-seat SUV
Audi|Q7.s: Built in Bratislava, delivered in France from November 2026; two plug-in hybrids (395 and 490 hp) are announced for the first quarter of 2027.

Audi|Q8.v: A facelifted luxury coupé SUV, very well built and spacious, here as a V6 plug-in hybrid. Its technology is judged behind the times: compromised boot, modest electric range and slow charging.
p: Vigorous acceleration from the V6 hybrid
m: Boot significantly reduced by the battery
Audi|Q8.q: Executives seeking a status SUV, with home charging
Audi|Q8.s: A second generation is confirmed, but not expected before 2028. MLB Evo underpinnings shared with the Q7. Rivals: BMW X6 and Mercedes GLE Coupé.

Audi|RS e-tron GT.v: Since the 2024 facelift, the most powerful series-production Audi: supercar acceleration, astonishing active suspension and very rapid charging, but limited emotion away from the track and a very high price.
m: Limited rear seats and boot (350 l)
Audi|RS e-tron GT.q: Wealthy enthusiasts seeking an exceptional electric GT
Audi|RS e-tron GT.s: Niche sales in France: 175 registrations in 2024, half as many as its cousin the Porsche Taycan.

Audi|RS3 Berline.v: The 400 hp five-cylinder in a three-box body: surgical handling, top-flight performance and a sound all its own, at the cost of tight rear space and boot.
m: Tight rear seats and boot (321 l)
High price and very expensive options
Audi|RS3 Berline.q: Enthusiasts wanting a very high-performance compact saloon
Audi|RS3 Berline.s: Facelifted in 2024: 0-100 km/h in 3.8 s and a Drift mode. Direct rival: the more powerful Mercedes-AMG CLA 45 S.

Audi|RS3 Sportback.v: Facelifted in 2024, the RS3 keeps its 400 hp five-cylinder, more endearing than the S3's engine, and a torque splitter that makes it incisive. A benchmark among sporty hatchbacks, priced accordingly.
p: Incisive chassis thanks to the torque splitter
m: High price and very expensive options
Small boot, smaller than the S3's
Cabin close to the A3's, a little drab
Audi|RS3 Sportback.q: Enthusiasts seeking a hatchback with an exceptional engine
Audi|RS3 Sportback.s: 2024 facelift: redesigned front end and diffuser, optimised torque splitter and Drift mode. Main rival: Mercedes-AMG A 45.

Audi|RS5.v: Heavy but surprisingly agile thanks to its electric rear differential, the plug-in hybrid RS5 combines comfort and effectiveness. It pays for its weight, a reduced boot and a muffled soundtrack.
p: Surprising agility thanks to the active rear differential
Brisk acceleration, very quiet electric running
m: Very heavy, and the agility doesn't hide it
Boot reduced by the battery, small fuel tank
Audi|RS5.q: Fans of versatile sports cars who charge at home and drive every day
Audi|RS5.s: No DC rapid charging: allow around 2 h 30 to 3 h on an 11 kW charger. A dedicated mode sends most of the torque to the rear.

Audi|RS5 Avant.v: This 639 hp estate is playful and comfortable, and disguises its weight well thanks to its electric rear differential. A small boot for an estate, a sometimes slow gearbox and an artificial soundtrack temper the picture.
p: Playful chassis, surprising traction and agility
m: Small boot for an estate, sloping floor
Gearbox slow to downshift when driven hard
Audi|RS5 Avant.q: Family men in a hurry who want a sporty estate and charge at home
Audi|RS5 Avant.s: The French weight-based malus tax adds around €15,000 to the bill, but according to L'argus the RS5 Avant remains much cheaper than a BMW M3 Touring.

Audi|S e-tron GT.v: Facelifted in 2024, the S e-tron GT now produces 591 hp, as much as the old RS. A fast, comfortable electric GT with very rapid charging, it suffers from an ageing interior and a high price.
Audi|S e-tron GT.q: Fans of fast, comfortable electric GTs
Audi|S e-tron GT.s: Active suspension available as an option (€8,500). 350-litre boot, plus an 85-litre front boot (frunk).

Audi|S3 Berline.v: In 2024 the S3 saloon gets the same upgrades as the Sportback: 333 hp, a rear torque splitter and a revised chassis. More playful and still versatile, it remains discreet but expensive.
p: Versatile and easy to live with
S tronic gearbox with quicker shifts
m: Less appealing sound than the RS3
High price and French malus tax
Audi|S3 Berline.q: Keen drivers who prefer a discreet saloon
Audi|S3 Berline.s: 2024 facelift: 333 hp and 420 Nm, 0-100 km/h in 4.7 s. Akrapovič exhaust available as an option.

Audi|S3 Sportback.v: Since 2024, the S3 has gained 23 hp and the RS3's rear torque splitter: more playful than before and still easy to live with, it remains a notch below the RS3 on track, braking included.
p: Versatile and easy to live with
S tronic gearbox with quicker shifts
m: Less appealing sound than the RS3
High price and French malus tax
Audi|S3 Sportback.q: Keen drivers wanting a fast hatchback they can use every day
Audi|S3 Sportback.s: 2024 facelift: 333 hp (+23 hp) and 420 Nm, rear torque splitter inherited from the RS3 and a Dynamic Plus mode that allows oversteer.

Audi|S5.v: The S5 pairs a 367 hp mild-hybrid V6 with quattro all-wheel drive: fast, well damped and refined, it is more GT than sports car, with uncommunicative steering.
Audi|S5.q: Fans of fast, comfortable everyday saloons
Audi|S5.s: The tailgate hides a 417-litre boot. Designated rival: the BMW M340i, judged more engaging by the British press.

Audi|S5 Avant.v: A versatile sporty estate: a 367 hp V6, quattro and careful sound insulation make it a fast, comfortable GT, but it is heavy (over 2 tonnes), quiet-sounding and has a smaller boot than before.
Audi|S5 Avant.q: Families in a hurry seeking a fast, discreet estate
Audi|S5 Avant.s: 448-litre boot, vs 495 litres for the old S4 Avant it replaces. Designated rival: BMW M340i Touring.

Audi|S6 Avant e-tron.v: A 503 hp electric estate, very comfortable thanks to standard air suspension and well equipped, but not very sporty for an S, heavy and considerably more expensive than the A6 Avant e-tron.
m: Very high price next to the A6 Avant e-tron
Boot smaller than the BMW i5 Touring's
Audi|S6 Avant e-tron.q: Families in a hurry wanting a fast, comfortable electric estate
Audi|S6 Avant e-tron.s: The first electric S6 Avant. Rivals: BMW i5 M60 Touring and Porsche Taycan Sport Turismo, both more dynamic.

Audi|S6 Sportback e-tron.v: The 503 hp version of the A6 e-tron: very fast, long-legged and well equipped, but less lively than a BMW i5 M60 and considerably more expensive than the A6 e-tron, for limited extra emotion.
p: Long range for a performance car
m: More GT than sports car, uncommunicative
Considerably more expensive than the A6 e-tron
Audi|S6 Sportback e-tron.q: Demanding drivers wanting a fast electric saloon
Audi|S6 Sportback e-tron.s: The artificial engine sound fails to convince. Rivals: the BMW i5 M60, judged more dynamic, and the Porsche Taycan.

Audi|S8.v: The 571 hp 4.0 TFSI V8 version of the A8: a very fast, very comfortable limousine, but at the end of its career, very expensive and heavily taxed.
m: Model at the end of its career
Steep depreciation, typical of the segment
Audi|S8.q: Fans of sporty limousines unconcerned by running costs
Audi|S8.s: Orders stopped in Germany in February 2026, with the end of production near. The electric replacement is not expected to be ready before 2029.

Audi|SQ2.v: The sporty version of the Q2, with 300 hp and quattro all-wheel drive: fast and effective, but expensive for a small SUV whose career is coming to an end.
p: Traction assured by quattro all-wheel drive
m: Price close to bigger, newer models
Audi|SQ2.q: Fans of small, high-riding performance cars, to be found among remaining stock
Audi|SQ2.s: The Q2 has been out of production since April 2026: only stock cars remain available.

Audi|SQ5.v: The 367 hp 3.0 TFSI V6 gives the SQ5 strong performance and good body control, but it is heavier than its predecessor and favours comfort over bite.
Audi|SQ5.q: Fans of fast, comfortable SUVs with a big budget
Audi|SQ5.s: The quattro system switches to a multi-plate clutch set-up. Rivals: BMW X3 M50 and Mercedes-AMG GLC 43.

Audi|SQ5 Sportback.v: The 367 hp V6 in the Sportback body: fast, agile and well built, but heavier than the old SQ5, less incisive and with the smallest boot in the Q5 range.
m: Smallest boot in the Q5 range
Expensive options, top of the Q5 range
Audi|SQ5 Sportback.q: Fans of sporty coupé SUVs with a big budget
Audi|SQ5 Sportback.s: 0-100 km/h in 4.5 s. The optional air suspension markedly improves comfort; quattro switches to a multi-plate clutch system.

Audi|SQ6 Sportback e-tron.v: Audi's most powerful electric coupé SUV is fast, hushed and well built, but lacks temperament for an S. L'argus prefers the cheaper Q6 quattro, or a Porsche Macan 4S.
m: Real-world range well below the claimed figure
Cluttered ergonomics, too much information on screen
Audi|SQ6 Sportback e-tron.q: Fans of fast, comfortable electric coupé SUVs
Audi|SQ6 Sportback e-tron.s: Roofline lowered by 37 mm compared with the Q6. The electric Porsche Macan, on the same underpinnings, is judged more fun to drive.

Audi|SQ6 e-tron.v: The most powerful version of the Q6 e-tron: the SQ6 accelerates hard and charges quickly, but testers find it more comfortable than sporty, with range and efficiency behind the other Q6 models.
m: Very high price next to the Q6 quattro
Audi|SQ6 e-tron.q: Drivers wanting a fast but discreet electric SUV
Audi|SQ6 e-tron.s: PPE platform shared with the electric Porsche Macan, which L'argus considers more dynamic for a similar price.

Audi|SQ7.v: The Q7 with a 507 hp 4.0 TFSI V8: astonishing performance for its size and great comfort, but this generation is on its way out and the French malus tax is prohibitive.
m: Generation replaced at the end of 2026
Audi|SQ7.q: Families who love big, high-performance SUVs
Audi|SQ7.s: The new (third-generation) Q7 can be ordered in France: V6 TDI at launch, deliveries in November 2026, plug-in hybrids in early 2027.

Audi|SQ8.v: The 507 hp twin-turbo V8 delivers first-rate performance and the build quality is superb. But the SQ8 remains heavy, thirsty and less polished than a Porsche Cayenne S, which the press rates higher.
m: Less agile and less polished than a Cayenne S
Audi|SQ8.q: Fans of big V8 SUVs unconcerned by running costs
Audi|SQ8.s: A second generation of the Q8 has been confirmed by Audi's management, but it is not expected before 2028.

Audi|e-tron GT.v: The entry-level version of the electric GT that is cousin to the Porsche Taycan: the longest-range model in the line-up, fast, precise and comfortable, but with tight rear seats and disappointing real-world efficiency.
Audi|e-tron GT.q: Fans of electric grand tourers with a substantial budget
Audi|e-tron GT.s: It shares its underpinnings with the Porsche Taycan, judged livelier and more engaging, while the Audi is the more comfortable of the two.

BMW|M2 CS.v: A more hardcore version of the M2, the CS gains power, sheds weight thanks to carbon fibre and shines on road and track alike. Its mass is still noticeable, the manual gearbox is gone and the bill, including the French malus tax, is considerable.
p: Around 30 kg saved thanks to carbon fibre
m: Mass still noticeable in fast corners
BMW|M2 CS.s: Built in Mexico, it is only available with an 8-speed automatic gearbox. L'argus recommends the standard M2 to those who want a manual gearbox and a gentler price.

BMW|M2 Coupé.v: Compact, rear-wheel drive and six-cylinder, the M2 remains an old-school sports car, very quick and still available with a manual gearbox. Its weight, close to that of an M4, and its price temper the enthusiasm.
p: Manual gearbox still on the price list
BMW|M2 Coupé.q: Keen drivers who want a compact rear-wheel-drive car
BMW|M2 Coupé.s: In France, the six-speed manual gearbox is offered at no extra cost; it saves about 25 kg but makes the car slightly slower.
BMW|M2 Coupé.x: The quicker 3.0 BMW M2 Auto 480 hp is the logical everyday choice; the Manual 480 hp, slightly slower and with less torque, offers a drive judged more authentic.

BMW|M3.v: A family saloon with supercar performance, the M3 Competition is judged one of the most complete four-door sports cars, especially for its chassis. On the downside: the grille, increased weight, firmness and high prices.
p: Reassuring all-wheel drive on slippery surfaces
Classy cabin, as roomy as a 3 Series
m: Very high price, options and running costs
BMW|M3.q: Enthusiasts who want a sports car that can serve every day
BMW|M3.s: At its launch in 2021, the M3 Competition was offered in rear-wheel drive, with M xDrive all-wheel drive then an option.

BMW|M3 Touring.v: The first M3 estate in history, the Touring combines spectacular performance, unexpected agility and a family-sized boot. Heavy, expensive and heavily taxed, it remains a rare beast.
p: Boot of around 500 l and estate practicality
m: Very high price and French malus tax
BMW|M3 Touring.q: Family men who love driving and have a substantial budget
BMW|M3 Touring.s: BMW waited more than twenty years before offering an M3 estate, whose suspension was recalibrated specifically for this body style.
BMW|M3 Touring.x: The 3.0 BMW M3 Competition M xDrive 530 hp is the most versatile. The CS xDrive 551 hp, more precise and better controlled, is noisier and far more expensive, without being much quicker on the road.

BMW|M4 Cabriolet.v: The M4 Convertible offers the M4's performance with the sky thrown in, plus unfailing traction. Heavier and less rigid than the coupé when pushed, it leaves the purists' vote to the latter.
m: Less rigid body than the coupé
Around 145 kg heavier than the coupé
BMW|M4 Cabriolet.s: Only M xDrive all-wheel drive is offered, but it can switch to a rear-wheel-drive mode with the stability control off.

BMW|M4 Coupé.v: A formidable sports coupé, the M4 Competition xDrive combines power, traction and versatility. Its grille, its mass and less feel than lighter sports cars temper the enthusiasm.
p: Usable every day as well as on track
BMW|M4 Coupé.q: Sports car enthusiasts comfortable with a high budget
BMW|M4 Coupé.s: Facelifted in 2024, it gains 20 hp and M4 CSL-inspired rear lights; the Competition is now sold only with M xDrive all-wheel drive.

BMW|M5.v: The M5 goes plug-in hybrid: colossal performance, comfort preserved and a genuine electric range. But its mass of nearly 2.5 tonnes and uncommunicative controls curb the enthusiasm.
BMW|M5.q: Wealthy enthusiasts who want an ultra-high-performance saloon
BMW|M5.s: Its boot shrinks to 466 litres, vs 520 for a regular 5 Series, and the battery charges only on AC (7.4 kW), with no rapid charging.

BMW|M5 Touring.v: The return of the M5 estate will delight connoisseurs: V8 hybrid powertrain, colossal performance and a more practical boot than the saloon's. The weight, close to 2.5 tonnes, remains the sore point.
m: Smaller boot than an Audi RS 6's
BMW|M5 Touring.q: Wealthy enthusiasts who want an ultra-high-performance estate
BMW|M5 Touring.s: The third M5 estate in history, it returns after an absence of around fifteen years, the previous one having left the range in 2010.

BMW|Série 1.v: A fourth generation with a much modernised interior, the 1 Series remains one of the most enjoyable premium hatchbacks to drive and proves frugal as a mild hybrid. Physical controls are scarce, and the boot is smaller on the hybrids.
p: Reasonable consumption as a mild hybrid
m: Boot reduced to 300 l on the hybrids
BMW|Série 1.q: Drivers seeking a modern, frugal premium hatchback
BMW|Série 1.s: The mild-hybrid versions lose about 80 litres of boot space (300 l vs 380 l). Caradisiac sees it more as a major facelift than an all-new generation.
BMW|Série 1.x: The frugal and sufficiently lively 1.5 BMW 120 170 hp suits everyday use. The very effective M135 xDrive 300 hp is more a fast, plush hatchback than a true sports car.

BMW|Série 2 Active Tourer.v: A well-built, spacious compact MPV that is pleasant to drive, the Active Tourer keeps a generous boot. Its firm suspension hurts comfort, especially on big wheels, and its screen's many sub-menus are confusing.
m: Firm ride, especially on big wheels
BMW|Série 2 Active Tourer.q: Families who value interior space over SUV looks
BMW|Série 2 Active Tourer.s: The seven-seat option of the previous generation, an advantage over the Mercedes B-Class, has not been carried over to this second generation.
BMW|Série 2 Active Tourer.x: The 2.0 BMW 218d 150 hp, measured at around 6 l/100 km by Motor1, still makes sense for high-mileage drivers; the 1.5 BMW 220i 170 hp returned 7.1 l/100 km with Caradisiac.

BMW|Série 2 Coupé.v: Still faithful to rear-wheel drive, the 2 Series Coupé appeals with its lively chassis and precise steering, from the 220i up to the six-cylinder M240i. Occasional-use rear seats, noticeable weight and costly options are the trade-offs.
p: Rear-wheel-drive layout, rare in the class
m: Firm on poor roads in M240i form
BMW|Série 2 Coupé.q: Keen drivers who want a compact coupé rather than an SUV
BMW|Série 2 Coupé.s: Unlike the 2 Series Gran Coupé, derived from the front-wheel-drive 1 Series, the Coupé sits on the rear-wheel-drive CLAR platform of the 3 and 4 Series.
BMW|Série 2 Coupé.x: The agile, comfortable 2.0 BMW 220i 184 hp sometimes lacks character. The far more powerful 3.0 BMW M240i xDrive 392 hp moves from GT to sports car, at the cost of firmer damping.

BMW|Série 2 Gran Coupé.v: Better presented, the 2 Series Gran Coupé offers precise steering, especially in 300 hp form, and a bigger boot than the 1 Series. Limited rear headroom, a boot with a small opening and convoluted menus count against it.
m: Saloon boot with a narrow opening
BMW|Série 2 Gran Coupé.q: Drivers who want a stylish compact premium saloon
BMW|Série 2 Gran Coupé.s: Its 430-litre boot is 50 litres larger than the 1 Series'. The 7-speed dual-clutch gearbox is standard.
BMW|Série 2 Gran Coupé.x: The 170 hp 220 lacks punch but is relaxed and comfortable; the muscular, precise M325 xDrive 300 hp only justifies its extra cost for spirited driving, and its sound disappoints Top Gear.

BMW|Série 3.v: A well-rounded premium saloon with exemplary build quality and roomy outer rear seats. The facelift has cost it in ergonomics and price, just as its replacement arrives.
p: 330e: up to 101 km of electric range (WLTP)
m: Climate control adjusted via the touchscreen
BMW|Série 3.q: Executives who want a well-built, versatile premium saloon
BMW|Série 3.s: The new 3 Series (G50), in petrol/diesel and plug-in hybrid form, is due to enter production in Munich in the second half of 2026: grounds for negotiating on the current car.
BMW|Série 3.x: The 320d appeals with its torque and economy, but in rear-wheel-drive form traction suffers in the wet, hence the appeal of the 320d xDrive; Caradisiac suggests the 318d to save money.

BMW|Série 3 Touring.v: A comfortable, quiet premium estate that is pleasant to drive, the facelifted 3 Series Touring remains very well built. Sharply higher prices and costly options.
m: Climate control moved to touch controls
Not the roomiest estate in its class
BMW|Série 3 Touring.q: Families who want a premium estate that is pleasant to drive
BMW|Série 3 Touring.s: The 2022 facelift replaced the physical climate controls with the touchscreen; diesels and six-cylinders get 48 V mild hybrid technology.

BMW|Série 4 Cabriolet.v: A polished four-seat convertible, the 4 Series combines a light, quick fabric roof, accomplished engines and room for four on short trips. A divisive grille, high weight and a narrow boot are the trade-offs.
p: Rear seats usable on short trips
Effective engines, led by the M440i
m: Small boot with a narrow opening
BMW|Série 4 Cabriolet.q: Convertible fans who travel as two or four
BMW|Série 4 Cabriolet.s: This generation swapped its predecessor's folding hard top for a fabric roof, retained in the early-2024 facelift.
BMW|Série 4 Cabriolet.x: According to Carbuyer, the lighter M440i xDrive is more agile than the M440d xDrive, which in turn uses less fuel.

BMW|Série 4 Coupé.v: A four-seat coupé that is enjoyable to drive, the 4 Series shines above all as the M440i, praised for its six-cylinder and quick steering. Its grille still divides opinion and the rear seats remain cramped.
BMW|Série 4 Coupé.q: Drivers who want a sporty coupé they can use every day
BMW|Série 4 Coupé.s: Facelifted in early 2024: revised light signature and bumpers, large screen and iDrive 8.5 interface, with the entry price slightly lowered at the time.
BMW|Série 4 Coupé.x: The M440i xDrive is the true sports car of the range; the quiet, refined 420d xDrive runs out of breath at high revs; Carbuyer finds the 420i agile and enjoyable.

BMW|Série 4 Gran Coupé.v: A coupé-styled saloon with a hatchback, the 4 Series Gran Coupé blends style, driving pleasure and practicality. Its grille divides opinion and the suspension is firm on poor surfaces.
p: Practical hatchback and folding rear bench
Polished engines, led by the M440i
BMW|Série 4 Gran Coupé.q: Drivers wanting an elegant yet practical saloon
BMW|Série 4 Gran Coupé.s: Facelifted in 2024 (on sale from July): revised grille and headlights, new steering wheel, no mechanical changes.
BMW|Série 4 Gran Coupé.x: What Car? recommends the 420i, smooth and quiet; the 420d xDrive, frugal and punchy at low revs, is noisy at idle; the M440i xDrive delivers top-drawer performance.

BMW|Série 5.v: A comfortable, quiet and well-built long-distance cruiser, the 5 Series is one of the benchmarks in its class, with a wide choice of powertrains. It is very large, and its controls rely heavily on the touchscreen.
p: Choice of diesel, hybrid or electric (i5)
m: Climate control run through the touchscreen
Comfort suffers with the M Sport pack and 20-inch wheels
BMW|Série 5.q: High-mileage drivers or executives wanting a premium long-distance saloon
BMW|Série 5.s: It shares its body with the electric i5: a rare saloon offered with a choice of diesel, plug-in hybrid and electric power.
BMW|Série 5.x: The 520d, frugal and quiet, remains the most sensible pick for high-mileage drivers but soon runs out of steam when driven hard; the 550e xDrive can be both a comfortable cruiser and a sports saloon.

BMW|Série 5 Touring.v: A premium long-distance estate, the 5 Series Touring carries over the saloon's comfort and refinement, with a choice of powertrains rarely seen in the segment. It is very large, and its controls rely heavily on the touchscreen.
p: Choice of diesel, hybrid or electric
m: Climate control run through the touchscreen
BMW|Série 5 Touring.q: High-mileage families wanting a premium estate
BMW|Série 5 Touring.s: Launched in May 2024, it is built in Dingolfing on the same line as its hybrid and fully electric (i5 Touring) versions.

BMW|Série 7.v: A remarkably refined luxury limousine, the 7 Series wins buyers over with its comfort and beautifully finished cabin. Its styling divides opinion; a facelifted version was unveiled in April 2026.
p: Comfort and refinement of the very highest order
BMW|Série 7.q: Executives or frequent travellers who are often driven in the back
BMW|Série 7.s: Facelift unveiled in April 2026: Panoramic Vision display spanning the width of the windscreen, redesigned dashboard, and hybrids claimed to cover 80 km on electric power.

BMW|X1.v: The X1 improves on build quality, equipment and boot space. Its touchscreen-centric ergonomics, slightly firm suspension and powertrains that divide opinion temper the picture.
p: Bigger boot, optional sliding rear bench
m: Basic functions buried in the touchscreen
Slightly firm suspension on broken roads
BMW|X1.q: Families wanting a versatile premium compact SUV
BMW|X1.s: According to L'argus, the combustion-engined X1 is due a facelift in summer 2027 and will stay in production until 2033.

BMW|X2.v: The X2 now sets itself apart from the X1 with a coupé-SUV silhouette and a bigger boot, on an equally well-finished base. A high price and comfort that suffers on big wheels dampen its appeal.
p: Generous boot for a coupé SUV
m: Brake pedal hard to modulate in town
BMW|X2.q: Style-conscious buyers of a premium compact SUV
BMW|X2.s: Its roof is 4 cm lower than the X1's, from which it borrows the dashboard and OS9 interface.
BMW|X2.x: The sDrive20i, smooth and unobtrusive in town, lacks sparkle on the open road; the M35i xDrive, one of the most fun compact SUVs according to Le Moniteur, is considered very expensive and less sharp than its predecessor.

BMW|X3.v: Very capable on the road and more comfortable than its predecessor according to most tests, the new X3 ranks among the most accomplished premium family SUVs. Cheap plastics and pricey options.
BMW|X3.q: Families seeking a versatile premium SUV for the open road
BMW|X3.s: The electric version is the iX3, built on the Neue Klasse platform and styled differently from the combustion-engined X3.
BMW|X3.x: The 20 xDrive is enough for everyday use but runs out of breath at high revs; the 30e xDrive is aimed mainly at fleets; the M50 xDrive, fast and precise, is considered the most accomplished version.

BMW|X5.v: The fifth-generation X5 impressed with its comfort and refinement during early prototype drives. Its plug-in hybrid versions, delivered from 2027, have yet to be tested; size and price are imposing.
p: Comfort and refinement praised in prototype form
BMW|X5.q: Well-off frequent travellers willing to wait until 2027 for a luxury hybrid SUV
BMW|X5.s: Built in Spartanburg (USA). Plug-in hybrids and the electric version arrive in early 2027; in France, the 50e is listed at the same price as the iX5 60.

BMW|XM.v: The second dedicated BMW M model after the M1, the XM handles surprisingly well for its mass according to L'argus and CAR. But it feels numb, the ride is harsh, and its weight and price count heavily against it.
BMW|XM.q: Wealthy buyers after a flamboyant, powerful SUV
BMW|XM.s: The range was cut in 2025 to two versions, 50e and Label, which now accept 11 kW charging.

BMW|Z4.v: A roadster with character, especially the M40i with its full-bodied, vocal six-cylinder. Capable chassis and quick-folding roof, but the model is bowing out with no announced successor.
BMW|Z4.q: Sports convertible fans who drive alone or as a couple
BMW|Z4.s: Z4 production ended in March 2026 with a Final Edition series: the last cars are being sold from stock, with no successor announced.

BMW|i4.v: An enjoyable, well-finished electric saloon, the i4 divides opinion on real-world range and rapid charging, both judged disappointing by Actu-Automobile. The new Neue Klasse i3 could eventually replace it.
m: Real-world range short of the claimed figure
BMW|i4.q: Drivers wanting a dynamic electric saloon
BMW|i4.s: BMW is launching the new electric i3 (Neue Klasse), of similar size: Top Gear reckons it could eventually push the i4 out of the line-up.
BMW|i4.x: Top Gear prefers the rear-wheel-drive eDrive35 and eDrive40, agile and enjoyable; the i4 M60 xDrive, much quicker, is firmer and less refined.

BMW|i5.v: The electric version of the 5 Series, the i5 shares its quietness and excellent handling, with rather firm damping. Average consumption, an average-sized boot and high prices temper the picture.
m: Rear centre seat compromised by the tunnel
High prices, quickly inflated by options
BMW|i5.q: High-mileage executives ready for an electric saloon
BMW|i5.s: It shares its body with the combustion-engined 5 Series, hence a pronounced central tunnel in the rear and no front boot.
BMW|i5.x: What Car? recommends the i5 eDrive40, which has less grip in the wet without adaptive suspension; the i5 M60 xDrive, the best-handling car in its class according to Top Gear, costs much more.

BMW|i5 Touring.v: A remarkably quiet and comfortable electric estate, the i5 Touring combines the practicality of a big boot with the refinement of the 5 Series. Modest real-world range, high weight and high prices.
BMW|i5 Touring.q: Families wanting a large premium electric estate
BMW|i5 Touring.s: One of the few electric estates on the market. An all-wheel-drive xDrive40 joined the eDrive40 and M60 in September 2024.
BMW|i5 Touring.x: The i5 eDrive40, cheaper and with slightly more range, is the best choice according to CAR and Top Gear, despite more body roll; the i5 M60 xDrive combines very high performance with remarkable refinement.

BMW|i7.v: An exceptionally refined electric limousine, the i7 is one of the benchmarks of electric luxury. The facelift unveiled in April 2026 promises improved range and charging.
BMW|i7.q: Executives seeking a top-end luxury electric limousine
BMW|i7.s: Facelifted in April 2026: claimed range of up to 720 km and rapid charging raised to 250 kW, still behind the Mercedes EQS.

BMW|iX.v: A very comfortable and quiet luxury electric SUV, the iX gained significantly in range and power with its 2025 facelift. Styling still divisive, imposing size and high prices.
p: Spacious cabin with a flat floor
BMW|iX.q: High-mileage drivers seeking a luxury electric SUV
BMW|iX.s: Facelifted in 2025 with new names (xDrive45, xDrive60, M70), more power and a WLTP range approaching 700 km for the xDrive60.
BMW|iX.x: The xDrive45, now punchy, is considered the most sensible choice; the xDrive60 has the longest range; the M70, firmer and sharper, prioritises performance at the expense of comfort.

BMW|iX1.v: The iX1 shares the X1's neat presentation and is lively in xDrive30 form. But its motorway range remains limited, its rapid charging is average and rear space is down on the combustion version.
p: Good balance of comfort and body control
m: Less rear space and boot than the X1
BMW|iX1.q: First-time premium electric SUV buyers who rarely do long journeys
BMW|iX1.s: A Neue Klasse-style facelift, borrowing the iX3's dashboard, is expected to go on sale in early 2027.

BMW|iX2.v: The electric version of the X2, the iX2 is agile, well insulated and practical with its 525-litre boot. Real-world range well below the claimed figure, poor visibility and firm suspension.
BMW|iX2.q: Buyers of a compact electric SUV with distinctive styling
BMW|iX2.s: Rapid charging peaks at 130 kW, or around 29 minutes for 10-80%, par for the class.

BMW|iX3.v: The first Neue Klasse model, the iX3 impresses with its efficiency, rapid charging and engaging drive, even if L'argus feels its weight holds it back. Some settings remain buried in menus.
m: Regeneration adjustable only via the screen
Feature-rich interface that takes time to learn
BMW|iX3.q: High-mileage drivers ready to switch to a premium electric SUV
BMW|iX3.s: It debuts the Panoramic iDrive display projected along the bottom of the windscreen and supports bidirectional charging (V2L, V2H, V2G).

BMW|iX5.v: The first electric X5, the iX5 aims for record range with its 141 kWh battery and very fast charging. Spacious, it weighs nearly 2.9 tonnes; tests of the production version are still to come.
p: Claimed range among the best on the market
Rapid charging claimed at up to 460 kW
m: Not yet tested in production form
BMW|iX5.q: Well-off high-mileage drivers wanting an electric SUV for long journeys
BMW|iX5.s: Due on sale from March 2027. Top speed limited to 210 km/h; a hydrogen version will later join the range.

BYD|Atto 2.v: A spacious, well-finished small SUV offered as an EV or plug-in hybrid at a keen price. The DM-i Boost approaches 100 km of real-world electric range and is more convincing than the EV; the drive lacks finesse.
p: Generous rear space for its size
Good build quality and equipment for the price
Plug-in hybrid with nearly 100 km of electric range
BYD|Atto 2.q: Families looking for a roomy small SUV at the best price
BYD|Atto 2.s: The DM-i version targets the Renault Captur E-Tech and Dacia Duster Hybrid. 6-year or 150,000 km warranty, battery 8 years or 250,000 km.
BYD|Atto 2.x: The DM-i Boost, the most recommended, approaches 100 km of real-world electric range; the Active, with its small battery, offers far less. The 64.8 kWh EV charges much faster than the small battery but is less appealing.

BYD|Atto 3 Evo.v: A thorough update of the Atto 3: rear-wheel drive, a bigger battery, much faster rapid charging and a front boot. But handling and ride on poor surfaces still trail its rivals.
p: Brisk acceleration, especially with all-wheel drive
m: Everyday settings buried in the screen
Noticeable wind noise on the motorway
BYD|Atto 3 Evo.q: Families wanting a powerful, fast-charging compact electric SUV
BYD|Atto 3 Evo.s: Replaces the Atto 3 launched in 2022: rear-wheel drive takes over from front-wheel drive. 6-year or 150,000 km warranty, battery 8 years or 250,000 km.
BYD|Atto 3 Evo.x: The rear-wheel-drive Design 313 hp has the best range and ample performance; the Excellence AWD 449 hp, much quicker and better equipped, is judged more stable on poor roads by Fleet News.

BYD|Dolphin G.v: A plug-in hybrid sold for the price of a conventional hybrid, with nearly 100 km of electric range in Boost form. Firm suspension, vague steering and cheap plastics remain its weak points.
p: Plug-in for the price of a conventional hybrid
BYD|Dolphin G.q: Drivers who charge at home and mostly drive in town and the suburbs
BYD|Dolphin G.s: On sale in France in 2026, it targets the hybrid Renault Clio and Toyota Yaris. BYD warranty of 6 years or 150,000 km.
BYD|Dolphin G.x: The DM-i Boost and its derivatives, with the larger battery, approach 100 km of real-world electric range and accept rapid charging; the Active, with its small battery, leans more on the petrol engine.

BYD|Dolphin Surf.v: A well-finished, well-equipped electric city car, with a lively 156 hp in top form. You have to put up with slow rapid charging, driver aids often judged intrusive and an unrefined drive.
BYD|Dolphin Surf.q: City dwellers wanting a well-equipped EV without needing long range
BYD|Dolphin Surf.s: BYD warranty of 6 years or 150,000 km, battery covered for 8 years or 250,000 km. A direct rival to the Renault 5 E-Tech.
BYD|Dolphin Surf.x: The Active, with its small battery, has a range judged tight even for suburban use; the Boost, with the larger battery and 88 hp, is the most sensible according to Automobile Propre; the Comfort 156 hp adds liveliness and equipment.

BYD|Seal.v: A fast, comfortable and well-equipped electric saloon, and a credible alternative to the Tesla Model 3. It falls short on rapid charging limited to 150 kW, a boot without a hatchback and too many touch controls.
BYD|Seal.q: Drivers wanting a fast, comfortable, well-equipped electric saloon
BYD|Seal.s: BYD warranty of 6 years or 150,000 km, Blade LFP battery covered for 8 years or 250,000 km. A rival to the Tesla Model 3 and Hyundai Ioniq 6.
BYD|Seal.x: The rear-wheel-drive Design, more efficient and cheaper, is considered the most rational choice; the Excellence AWD mainly adds sports-car acceleration and adaptive dampers.

BYD|Seal 6.v: A plug-in hybrid saloon built for long journeys, with a long total range and a very favourable price-to-equipment ratio. Firm damping, road noise and slow charging count against it.
p: Long combined range for long journeys
BYD|Seal 6.q: High-mileage drivers wanting a frugal, well-equipped saloon at a keen price
BYD|Seal 6.s: A rare plug-in hybrid saloon at this price, also available as the Seal 6 Touring estate, whose boot is easier to access. BYD warranty of 6 years or 150,000 km.
BYD|Seal 6.x: The Boost, with its small battery, does not accept rapid charging and offers roughly half the electric range; the pricier Comfort is considered the more sensible choice.

BYD|Seal 6 Touring.v: A spacious, well-equipped and frugal plug-in hybrid estate, priced below its European rivals. Average sound insulation, modest acceleration and limited rapid charging dampen its appeal.
m: Sound insulation could be better (wind, engine)
BYD|Seal 6 Touring.q: Families wanting a roomy, economical estate without going electric
BYD|Seal 6 Touring.s: Priced below European plug-in hybrid estates. Ride comfort divides the press. BYD warranty of 6 years or 150,000 km.
BYD|Seal 6 Touring.x: The Boost, the cheapest, makes do with a small battery and no rapid charging; the Comfort roughly doubles the electric range and adds rapid charging, hence What Car's preference.

BYD|Seal U.v: A comfortable, quiet and well-finished family SUV, offered as an EV or plug-in hybrid. Its very soft suspension and vague steering leave it ill at ease as soon as the road starts to twist.
m: Boot tight for an SUV of this size
BYD|Seal U.q: Families who put comfort and equipment before driving pleasure
BYD|Seal U.s: The lighter, cheaper Sealion 5 DM-i competes with it within BYD's own range. 6-year or 150,000 km warranty.
BYD|Seal U.x: Among the hybrids, the Boost is enough according to CAR; the 324 hp Design AWD, much quicker, adds no equipment and uses more fuel. The electric version was not assessed here.

BYD|Sealion 5.v: A plug-in hybrid family SUV with an aggressive price-to-equipment ratio, comfortable and well insulated. Dull driving, slow charging and high motorway consumption dampen its appeal.
p: Price well below comparable European SUVs
BYD|Sealion 5.q: Budget-conscious families who mostly drive on electric power day to day
BYD|Sealion 5.s: 216 kg lighter than the Seal U DM-i, it is less penalised by France's weight-based taxation. BYD warranty of 6 years or 150,000 km.
BYD|Sealion 5.x: The Design, slightly pricier than the Comfort, adds a bigger battery, hence more electric range, and useful equipment (360° camera, powered tailgate): the extra cost is considered justified.

BYD|Sealion 7.v: A very well-equipped electric coupé SUV with an upmarket cabin and spacious rear seats. High consumption, poorly judged suspension and unconvincing dynamics put it behind the Tesla Model Y.
m: High consumption that eats into real-world range
BYD|Sealion 7.q: Buyers wanting an upmarket, well-equipped electric SUV
BYD|Sealion 7.s: 6-year or 150,000 km warranty, battery 8 years or 250,000 km. Against the Tesla Model Y, it bets on equipment rather than efficiency.
BYD|Sealion 7.x: The rear-wheel-drive Comfort is judged playful by Presse-citron; the very fast 530 hp AWD shows tricky cornering behaviour for its 2.4 tonnes according to L'argus.

BYD|Tang.v: A large, powerful and well-finished seven-seat electric SUV, facelifted in 2024 with a bigger battery. Its 2.5 tonnes take their toll on consumption, braking feel and agility.
m: Very high consumption, especially on the motorway
BYD|Tang.q: Large families wanting seven seats and plenty of power in an EV
BYD|Tang.s: Facelifted in 2024: bigger battery and rapid charging raised to 170 kW; press tests cover the previous version. 6-year or 150,000 km warranty.

Citroën|C3.v: The fourth-generation C3 relies on a keen price, genuine ride comfort and a high driving position. Basic finish, average sound insulation and body roll reflect its positioning.
Citroën|C3.q: Budget buyers wanting a comfortable city car
Citroën|C3.s: A European Car of the Year 2025 finalist; its latest-generation 1.2 uses a timing chain instead of the wet belt.
Citroën|C3.x: The cheaper 1.2 Turbo 100 hp gets noisy under load; the 110 hp hybrid, with automatic gearbox, is more frugal and more relaxing in town, but remains a mild hybrid.

Citroën|C3 Aircross.v: The C3 Aircross offers lots of space and genuine comfort for its price, with an occasional-use seven-seat option. Budget finish, light sound insulation and a hybrid gearbox that is jerky in town betray its positioning.
p: Space and comfort for the price
m: Wind and road noise on the motorway
Slow hybrid gearbox, jerky in town
Citroën|C3 Aircross.q: Budget-conscious families wanting a spacious compact SUV
Citroën|C3 Aircross.s: Its hybrid uses a 1.2 with a timing chain, not the much-criticised wet belt. As a seven-seater, the third row is for occasional use and the boot drops to 40 litres.
Citroën|C3 Aircross.x: The 1.2 Turbo 100 hp with manual gearbox is the entry point; the 145 hp hybrid, more frugal and more at ease on fast roads, is judged better suited to family use despite its slow gearbox in town.

Citroën|C4.v: The C4 prioritises comfort thanks to its suspension with hydraulic bump stops and its plush seats. Handling remains staid, rear visibility limited and the infotainment slow.
m: Boot on the small side of average
Citroën|C4.q: Drivers who put comfort before driving dynamics
Citroën|C4.s: Facelifted in early 2025, with thicker seat foam. Its hybrid versions get the latest-generation 1.2 with a timing chain.
Citroën|C4.x: What Car prefers the 110 hp hybrid, the best compromise; Complete Car finds the 145 hp hybrid livelier and more relaxed.

Citroën|C4 X.v: A saloon with a raised silhouette, the C4 X offers a big boot, careful comfort and good sound insulation. Handling remains staid, rear visibility limited and the infotainment dated.
m: Rear headroom tight for tall passengers
Citroën|C4 X.q: Drivers wanting a comfortable saloon with a generous boot
Citroën|C4 X.s: Facelifted in early 2025, with no notable change at the rear or in the cabin. A saloon boot with no hatchback, awkward for bulky items.

Citroën|C5 Aircross.v: The new C5 Aircross relies on benchmark comfort, record space and a wide choice of powertrains, from hybrid to electric. A finish below that of its predecessor and modest dynamics temper the picture.
m: No more three sliding rear seats
Citroën|C5 Aircross.q: Families who prioritise comfort and space
Citroën|C5 Aircross.s: Built in Rennes on the Peugeot 3008's STLA Medium platform, it takes over the slot of the C5 X, withdrawn from Europe. A European Car of the Year 2026 finalist.
Citroën|C5 Aircross.x: The 145 hp hybrid, a mere mild hybrid, is considered limited; the plug-in hybrid is frugal with a full battery but noisy under load; the electric is the most pleasant version.

Citroën|C5 X.v: A comfortable, quiet long-distance cruiser, the C5 X never found its audience in Europe. Only one powertrain remains and resale looks tricky.
Citroën|C5 X.q: High-mileage drivers who prioritise comfort on long journeys
Citroën|C5 X.s: Built in China, it has not been produced for Europe since 2025 and will have no successor: only stock cars remain available.

Citroën|ë-C3.v: One of the most affordable electric city cars on the market, the ë-C3 appeals with its comfort and space. Tight range outside town, light sound insulation and a basic finish limit its versatility.
p: More space and a bigger boot than the Dacia Spring
m: Rapid charging optional, and only 30 kW on the Urban Range
Citroën|ë-C3.q: City dwellers wanting to go electric on a budget
Citroën|ë-C3.s: A European Car of the Year 2025 finalist, it is built in Europe, in Slovakia.
Citroën|ë-C3.x: The Urban Range, the cheapest, is fine for commuting but needs the rapid-charging option to venture out of town; the Comfort Range, with more range, is more versatile.

Citroën|ë-C3 Aircross.v: The electric version of the C3 Aircross offers lots of space and comfort at a keen price. Modest range and power, however, make it better suited to everyday trips than long journeys.
Citroën|ë-C3 Aircross.q: Families wanting a spacious electric SUV for local use
Citroën|ë-C3 Aircross.s: The 44 kWh battery was dropped in late 2025 for lack of demand, leaving only the 54 kWh. Unlike the combustion version, there is no seven-seat option.
Citroën|ë-C3 Aircross.x: The Extended Range, now the only version listed according to Actu Automobile, is recommended by Auto Express for its far more usable range; the small battery disappoints as soon as you leave town.

Citroën|ë-C4.v: Facelifted, the ë-C4 remains a comfort-focused electric hatchback, thanks to its hydraulic bump stops and thick seats. Modest motorway range and dated infotainment dampen its appeal.
Citroën|ë-C4.q: Drivers wanting a comfortable electric hatchback
Citroën|ë-C4.s: Facelifted in 2025 (shown at the 2024 Paris Motor Show): new lighting signature, larger digital instrument cluster on Max, and thicker seat foam.
Citroën|ë-C4.x: The 156 hp, with its larger battery, offers more range and much brisker overtaking than the 136 hp, which is reserved for entry-level trims.

Citroën|ë-C4 X.v: The saloon version of the ë-C4 adds a big boot to the hatchback's comfort and quietness. A dull interior, awkward infotainment and modest range limit its appeal.
p: Big boot, though awkward to access
Citroën|ë-C4 X.q: Drivers wanting a comfortable, practical electric saloon
Citroën|ë-C4 X.s: Facelifted in 2025 alongside the C4: new front end and lighting signature, thicker seat foam. The rear end is unchanged.
Citroën|ë-C4 X.x: The 156 hp, with the larger battery, is the recommended choice for range; the cheaper 136 hp also charges at up to 100 kW.

Cupra|Born.v: The sportier twin of the ID.3, the Born offers polished handling and solid range with the larger battery. The 2026 facelift fixes the ergonomics, but boot space and price remain its weak points.
p: Solid range with the larger battery
m: Rear seats compromised by the floor
Cupra|Born.q: Drivers wanting an enjoyable electric hatchback
Cupra|Born.s: Facelifted in 2026: larger digital instrument cluster, proper steering-wheel buttons, One Pedal mode and rear air vents.
Cupra|Born.x: The 190 hp with the small battery lacks punch; the Endurance 230 hp, with the large battery for little extra cost, is the sensible choice; the VZ 325 hp, firmer and fun, is expensive.

Cupra|Formentor.v: A compact SUV with bold styling, the Formentor appeals with its dynamic handling and rear space. Firm damping, a modest boot and high prices temper the picture.
p: Bold styling, sharpened by the facelift
Cupra|Formentor.q: Keen drivers wanting an SUV with bold styling
Cupra|Formentor.s: Facelifted in 2024: revised front end, 12.9-inch central screen, five-cylinder dropped. It then accounted for 60% of Cupra's sales in France.
Cupra|Formentor.x: The 1.5 eTSI Hybrid DSG 150 hp, frugal and the cheapest, is the sensible choice but lacks character and its DSG gearbox is sluggish; the eHybrid versions lose a lot of boot space.

Cupra|Leon.v: A hatchback with a capable chassis, the Cupra Leon broke away from Seat with its 2024 facelift and offers fast VZ versions and a long-range plug-in hybrid. The base 1.5 lacks character and prices are high.
p: Plug-in hybrid with good electric range
Cupra|Leon.q: Keen drivers wanting a versatile hatchback
Cupra|Leon.s: Facelifted in 2024: “shark nose” front end, 12.9-inch screen and, on the plug-in hybrid, a bigger battery and 50 kW rapid charging.
Cupra|Leon.x: The 1.5 eTSI Hybrid DSG 150 hp, smooth and frugal, lacks character for a Cupra; the eHybrid DSG 272 hp, just as agile and more comfortable, is the testers' favourite; the 2.0 TSI versions focus on sportiness.

Cupra|Leon Sportstourer.v: The Leon estate combines a big boot with a dynamic chassis and plug-in hybrids with longer electric range since 2024. The ride remains firm and the bill high.
p: Plug-in hybrids with good electric range
m: Smaller boot on the plug-in hybrid
Cupra|Leon Sportstourer.q: Active families wanting a sporty yet practical estate
Cupra|Leon Sportstourer.s: Facelifted in 2024 like the hatchback (“shark nose” front end, 12.9-inch screen), it sits on the MQB platform of the Volkswagen Golf Estate.
Cupra|Leon Sportstourer.x: The 1.5 eTSI Hybrid DSG 150 hp, smooth and frugal, lacks character; the eHybrid DSG 272 hp, agile and with good electric range, is more convincing but cuts the boot from 620 to 470 litres.

Cupra|Raval.v: An electric city car with bold styling, the Raval debuts the Volkswagen Group's small-EV platform. Testers praise its agility, braking and space; the VZ adds little over the Endurance.
Cupra|Raval.q: Young city dwellers wanting an EV with a sporty character
Cupra|Raval.s: Developed under Cupra's lead, its platform is shared with the Volkswagen ID. Polo and ID. Cross and the Skoda Epiq.
Cupra|Raval.x: The Endurance 211 hp, with firm but well-controlled suspension, is judged the best choice; the VZ 226 hp adds adaptive dampers for barely better performance.

Cupra|Tavascan.v: An electric coupé SUV with bold design, the Tavascan stands out for its original interior, good cabin space and lively VZ version. Weight, touch controls and the VZ's price count against it.
Cupra|Tavascan.q: Drivers wanting an electric SUV with bold styling
Cupra|Tavascan.s: Built in China by Volkswagen Anhui, it has been exempt since 2026 from the EU's additional tariff in exchange for a minimum price and a sales cap.
Cupra|Tavascan.x: The rear-wheel-drive Endurance 286 hp, with more range and much cheaper, keeps most of the character according to Automobile Propre; the livelier VZ 4Drive 340 hp comes at a high price.

Cupra|Terramar.v: A compact SUV derived from the Tiguan, the Terramar has carefully crafted styling and presentation, and its plug-in hybrids offer useful electric range. High prices and a smaller boot on the hybrids.
p: Plug-in hybrid with good electric range
m: Smaller boot on the plug-in hybrid
Heavy and prone to understeer as a hybrid
Cupra|Terramar.q: Families wanting a compact SUV with a sporty character
Cupra|Terramar.s: It uses the Volkswagen Tiguan's underpinnings, with a lower silhouette. The plug-in hybrid exceeds 100 km of official electric range.
Cupra|Terramar.x: The eHybrid DSG 272 hp, the most sensible according to Car Magazine, loses boot space and feels heavy in corners; the lighter 1.5 eTSI Hybrid DSG 150 hp lacks verve according to L'argus.

DS Automobiles|DS 3.v: Facelifted, the DS 3 appeals with its comfort and an electric version with much greater range. But rear space remains tight and prices are very high for its size.
p: Ride comfort and smoothness in town
Much greater range for the EV
DS Automobiles|DS 3.q: City drivers who put comfort and style before space
DS Automobiles|DS 3.s: The facelift gave the EV a new French-built 156 hp motor and an extra 84 km of WLTP range.
DS Automobiles|DS 3.x: The Hybrid 145 hp, frugal and comfortable, suffers from jerky gearchanges at low speed; the E-Tense 156 hp, quiet in town, costs much more and loses range quickly on the motorway.

DS Automobiles|DS 7.v: The facelifted DS 7 has a well-crafted interior and offers powerful all-wheel-drive plug-in hybrids. A noisy petrol engine and the firm suspension of the 360 hp version temper the picture; the N°7 succeeds it.
m: Suspension too firm on the 360 hp version
Noisy petrol engine, high real-world consumption
DS Automobiles|DS 7.q: Drivers wanting a French premium plug-in hybrid SUV
DS Automobiles|DS 7.s: Facelifted in 2022, it is being replaced by the DS N°7, due in October 2026, which drops diesel and plug-in hybrid power.
DS Automobiles|DS 7.x: The all-wheel-drive 300 hp, with adaptive suspension, favours comfort; the lowered and stiffened all-wheel-drive 360 hp is quicker but judged too firm for a DS.

DS Automobiles|N°4.v: Facelifted and renamed in 2025, the former DS 4 relies on refined presentation, a good balance of comfort and dynamics, and a multi-energy line-up. Tight boot and many options.
p: Good balance of comfort and dynamics
Petrol, plug-in hybrid and electric line-up
DS Automobiles|N°4.q: Drivers wanting a comfort-focused French premium hatchback
DS Automobiles|N°4.s: The DS 4 was facelifted and renamed N°4 in 2025, gaining its first fully electric version, with 213 hp.
DS Automobiles|N°4.x: The 225 hp plug-in hybrid, quicker and with more electric range, loses boot space compared with the 1.2 Hybrid 145 hp; the E-Tense Electric 213 hp falls short on range and charging.

DS Automobiles|N°7.v: More accomplished than the old DS 7, the N°7 appeals with its comfort, quietness, finish and the range of the Long Range EV. The 145 hp hybrid is unrefined; charging and infotainment lag behind.
p: Long range from the Long Range EV
m: Rapid charging lags behind (400 V, 160 kW)
DS Automobiles|N°7.q: Families looking for a comfortable, well-finished French premium SUV
DS Automobiles|N°7.s: Built in Italy. Non-reclining rear bench, no front boot on the EV, and the hybrid can tow only 650 kg. A plug-in hybrid is planned for 2027.
DS Automobiles|N°7.x: The E-Tense FWD Long Range 245 hp offers the best range and brisk acceleration; the cheaper 1.2 Hybrid 145 hp lacks pull under load and uses nearly 7 l/100 km in real-world driving.

DS Automobiles|N°8.v: The N°8 convinces with its comfort, quietness and a range among the best on the market. But rear space disappoints for its size, some of the finish is patchy and prices are ambitious.
p: Range among the best on the market
m: Disappointing rear seats for its size
High price, charging limited to 160 kW
DS Automobiles|N°8.q: High-mileage drivers wanting a large, comfort-focused premium EV
DS Automobiles|N°8.s: Built in Melfi (Italy) on the STLA Medium platform; its battery is made in Douvrin and its motor in Trémery.
DS Automobiles|N°8.x: The FWD Long Range 245 hp, the most popular, offers the longest range. The AWD Long Range 350 hp, heavier and thirstier, is livelier and surprisingly fun to drive.

Dacia|Bigster.v: The Duster's big brother, the Bigster offers the space of a family SUV for the price of a compact SUV. Comfortable and frugal as a hybrid, it falls short on hard plastics, motorway wind noise and a sometimes slow gearbox.
p: Family-SUV space at a keen price
m: Hybrid gearbox sometimes slow to respond when accelerating
Hard plastics and no seven-seat version
Dacia|Bigster.q: Families wanting a big, practical SUV without paying for a premium badge
Dacia|Bigster.s: Built in Romania. The Hybrid 155 is front-wheel drive only: the 4x4 version makes do with mild hybrid assistance.
Dacia|Bigster.x: The 1.8 Hybrid 155 hp is the most frugal and the most pleasant in town. For rough terrain, the press points towards the 1.2 Mild Hybrid 4X4 130 hp, which forgoes full hybrid power.

Dacia|Duster.v: A more modern, better-equipped third generation, the Duster remains one of the most affordable SUVs with a genuine 4x4 version. Hard plastics, unremarkable performance and a hybrid gearbox that could be better are its limits.
Dacia|Duster.q: Families or rural buyers wanting a tough, affordable SUV, with 4x4 if needed
Dacia|Duster.s: The range was expanded in 2026 with a Hybrid-G 150 version combining mild hybrid assistance and LPG. 3-year warranty, extendable to 7 years.
Dacia|Duster.x: The 1.6 Hybrid 140 hp is the most frugal but its gearbox lacks responsiveness. The 1.2 Mild Hybrid 4x4 130 hp, manual only, gains ground clearance. The 1.0 Eco-G 100 hp remains the entry-level version.

Dacia|Jogger.v: The only seven-seat estate at this price, roomy and versatile, it appeals to large families. Facelifted in 2026, it gains a livelier, more frugal hybrid, but sound insulation and driving pleasure still lag behind.
p: Seven seats for the price of a city car
Hybrid frugal in town, less so on the motorway
m: Hybrid powertrain noisy under heavy load
Dacia|Jogger.q: Large families on a tight budget who need seven seats
Dacia|Jogger.s: Facelifted in early 2026: new front end, Hybrid 155 and Eco-G 120 (LPG, automatic available) replacing the Hybrid 140 and Eco-G 100. 3-year warranty, extendable to 7 years.
Dacia|Jogger.x: The hybrid, frugal in town, struggles on the motorway and in the mountains; L'argus finds the 1.0 TCe 110 hp and 1.0 Eco-G 100 hp at least as pleasant. The facelift brings a livelier, more frugal Hybrid 155.

Dacia|Sandero.v: Europe's best-selling car in 2025, the facelifted Sandero offers one of the best value-for-money packages on the market and an LPG version with long range. Firm suspension and an engine that gets noisy when accelerating hold it back.
p: Value for money among the best
Dacia|Sandero.q: Budget buyers wanting a roomy new car
Dacia|Sandero.s: Facelifted in late 2025: TCe 100 replacing the TCe 90, Eco-G 120 offered with an automatic gearbox, screen up to 10 inches. 3-year warranty, extendable to 7 years.

Dacia|Sandero Stepway.v: The rugged-look version of the Sandero, with SUV styling and raised ground clearance for a modest premium. It inherits the city car's price and space advantages, along with its firm suspension and noisy engine.
p: SUV look for a modest premium
Value for money among the best
Dacia|Sandero Stepway.q: Budget-conscious families wanting an SUV look and space
Dacia|Sandero Stepway.s: Facelift unveiled in late 2025 (direct-injection TCe 110, automatic Eco-G 120). A 155 hp hybrid version is announced for late 2026.

Dacia|Spring.v: A bigger, better-equipped second generation, based on the Renault Twingo and built in Europe. It remains one of the cheapest new EVs, but no road test has been published yet.
p: Among the lowest prices for an EV
European production, helping eligibility for incentives
m: Little track record: launched in September 2026
Dacia|Spring.q: City dwellers looking for a simple, cheap EV for everyday use
Dacia|Spring.s: Shares 75% of its parts with the Twingo E-Tech, built in the same Novo Mesto plant (Slovenia). Orders opened on 8 September 2026.

Fiat|500.v: The petrol 500 returns on the wider, more stable base of the 500e, at an attractive entry price. But its slow 65 hp 1.0, barely helped by a 12 V mild hybrid system, largely confines it to town.
p: Steering wheel now adjustable for reach
Greater stability thanks to the 500e base
m: Performance among the most modest on the market
Fiat|500.q: City drivers attached to the 500's style who aren't ready to go electric
Fiat|500.s: Built at Mirafiori (Turin) alongside the 500e, it reuses the previous generation's naturally aspirated 12 V mild hybrid 1.0.

Fiat|500e.v: The 500e retains its retro charm, its liveliness in town and a well-executed infotainment system. But range, boot and rear seats remain limited, for a list price judged high against the Renault 5.
p: Brisk acceleration and quietness in town
m: High list price compared with the Renault 5
Fiat|500e.q: Style-conscious city drivers who mostly stay in town
Fiat|500e.s: The battery is guaranteed for 8 years or 160,000 km. In spring 2026, Fiat offered big discounts on the 500e, which could be combined with the French EV incentive.

Fiat|500e Cabrio.v: The fabric-roof version of the 500e keeps its style, quietness and liveliness in town, with surprising comfort. A cramped boot, limited rear seats and tight range outside town remain its limits.
m: Cramped rear seats, awkward to reach
Fiat|500e Cabrio.q: City drivers wanting open-top electric motoring
Fiat|500e Cabrio.s: The battery is guaranteed for 8 years or 160,000 km.

Fiat|600.v: Much cheaper than the 600e, the 600 hybrid appeals with its styling and price. A disappointing finish, tight rear space and jerkiness in town limit its appeal.
Fiat|600.q: Small SUV buyers wanting an affordable hybrid
Fiat|600.s: The 48 V hybrid integrates a 21 kW electric motor into the six-speed dual-clutch gearbox.
Fiat|600.x: Tested before the power increase, the entry-level version, now the 1.2 Hybrid 110 hp, is enough according to L'argus; the most powerful, now the 1.2 Hybrid 145 hp, barely justifies its extra cost.

Fiat|600e.v: The 600e is versatile, comfortable and easy to manoeuvre in town, with decent range. Uncommunicative steering, mediocre plastics and a hefty list price count against it.
m: High list price against the competition
Fiat|600e.q: Urban drivers looking for a compact electric SUV
Fiat|600e.s: Rapid charging limited to 100 kW (20-80% in 27 minutes). In spring 2026, Fiat offered big discounts on the 600e, which could be combined with the French EV incentive.

Fiat|Grande Panda.v: With its successful neo-retro styling, the Grande Panda offers lots of space for its size and keen prices as both a hybrid and an EV. Hard plastics and a hybrid gearbox that hesitates when accelerating temper the picture.
Fiat|Grande Panda.q: Families looking for a spacious, low-cost city car
Fiat|Grande Panda.s: Built in Kragujevac (Serbia). The hybrid combines a 110 hp 1.2 turbo, a 48 V battery and a six-speed dual-clutch gearbox.
Fiat|Grande Panda.x: The 1.2 Hybrid 110 hp offers more space and a boot around 50 litres bigger than the 113 hp EV (44 or 54 kWh battery), which stands out for its built-in charging cable, handy with a wallbox.

Fiat|Pandina.v: Endearing and easy to manoeuvre, the Pandina (formerly the Panda) shows its age: dated design, limited performance and a very poor Euro NCAP rating. Next to the Grande Panda, it only makes sense with a hefty discount.
Fiat|Pandina.q: Small budgets looking for a simple new city car
Fiat|Pandina.s: Renamed Pandina, it is built in Pomigliano d'Arco (Italy); production is guaranteed until at least 2030.

Fiat|Tipo.v: A spacious and cheap family saloon, but ageing in terms of safety, technology and perceived quality. Production ended in 2026, with no direct replacement.
p: Very low price for the space offered
Fiat|Tipo.q: High-mileage drivers on a small budget looking for a diesel saloon
Fiat|Tipo.s: Production ended in late June 2026 in Bursa (Turkey). Fiat has no direct replacement planned; available while stocks last.
